"So I wonder how many planes are taking off today in the US that are over weight simply because so many more people today are >190 lb"

None. Maximum take-off weight is a structural limit on the aircraft and does not change. Most commercial aircraft never approach this number because the Maximum Allowed Takeoff Weight (accounting for things like altitude, runway length, and flap settings) is usually lower. Violating the later is a hefty fine. Violating the former means you kill everyone onboard.

Passenger weight is all based on averages and statistics, but they're calculated so that the number on the load sheet will always be within 1% of the actual number. If it's any more than 1% above, the captain will make sure it's addressed before leaving the gate.

Simply put, if there are too many fatties on the plane, the problem will be rectified before the doors close, because above all else, the safe operation of the aircraft is the flight crew's primary responsibility.
